RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The all-male panel by itself proves little — it's common in economics and is a structural artefact more often than evidence of intent. Don't lead with it.

Your stronger point is the substantive one: on paper you outrank him on every stated academic criterion. That makes the weight given to "industry experience" the decisive question. If it wasn't in the advertised criteria, or wasn't weighted this way for you, that's a concrete procedural problem — and one you can actually test.

So: chase the written explanation (cite your legal/collective-agreement right to it, with a deadline). Ask for the criteria, weightings and scores. Mention panel composition only as context if the reasons turn out thin or shifting.
